title: C. elegans neuron classes with shorter connectome walks to body-wall muscle encode locomotion more strongly in two whole-brain data sets, beyond rewired-wiring nulls
abstract: Question: does the position of a neuron class in the connectome predict how strongly its activity encodes locomotion in freely moving C. elegans? Approach: for each class we calculated the expected random-walk steps to body-wall muscle in the Cook 2019 connectome (muscle distance). We fitted blocked, cross-validated ridge models of locomotion for 3,548 NeuroPAL-identified neurons in 40 off-food animals (Atanas 2023) and 814 neurons in 8 on-food animals (Dag 2023). Results: classes with a shorter muscle distance encoded locomotion more strongly (Spearman rho = -0.49, 58 classes, p = 0.0001; rho = -0.40, 54 classes, p = 0.003). Strength-preserving rewired connectomes gave mean rho near 0. Rewiring that kept every direct muscle synapse gave mean rho of -0.25 and -0.27, and the real value was stronger than 100% and 96.2% of 1,000 such nulls. After control for degree and direct muscle synapses, partial rho was -0.36 and -0.30. After control for degree, cell type, number of animals and label confidence, partial rho was -0.25 in each data set (p = 0.06 and 0.07). In interneurons only, rho was -0.40 and -0.41 (p = 0.03). Cross-animal transfer of encoding models also decreased with muscle distance, but within-animal encoding strength fully explained this (partial rho = +0.05 and +0.03). Limitations: across-class correlation, not a causal test; cell type explains part of the relation; nerve-ring-only Witvliet 2021 connectomes gave weaker relations of the same sign; on-food animals moved little; linear models with fixed time filters.

display.caption: Class locomotion encoding (mean clipped cross-validated R2) against random-walk steps to body-wall muscle in the Cook 2019 connectome, for 58 classes off food (Atanas 2023) and 54 classes on food (Dag 2023). Colour and marker show the Cook cell type.

Spearman rho between muscle distance and locomotion encoding in 1,000 strength-preserving rewired connectomes (blue) and 1,000 connectomes with only neuron-neuron contacts rewired and direct muscle synapses kept (orange). Black line: real connectome.

Spearman and partial Spearman rho of muscle distance with locomotion encoding and with cross-animal transfer, under different controls, in the two data sets. Bars show 95% class bootstrap intervals for the uncontrolled tests; p values at right.
